discussion_comments.comment_body: **blocking:** Prefixing every function name exceeds Meta Responses' 64-character tool-name limit for valid 64-character tools. `createMCPToolName()` caps MCP registry keys at exactly 64 (`packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/tool-bridge.ts:511-533`, citing Meta's HTTP 400); e.g. `mcp__long_server_name_tool_name_tool_name_tool_name_too_139vuzq6` becomes 65 characters here. A Muse session with that MCP tool now gets `name must be at most 64 characters` on every turn instead of the intended attestation fix. The wire-name mapping needs to keep names within the host limit without breaking call/replay lookup.

Fixed in e2175189ea. `muse-code.kdl` now sets `tool-call-name-max-length 64` on `openai-responses`, scoped by provider and API so it outranks the 128 Responses default. `encodeResponsesToolName` leaves a name unprefixed when `_` + name would exceed that limit. The blocked names are short, so a 64-character MCP name does not need the prefix.

Returned calls now map back through a wire-name table built from the declared tools (`responsesToolNamesByWire`), instead of by removing a leading `_`. An unprefixed long name and a tool whose own name starts with `_` both dispatch to the right tool. Two tools that would share one wire name fail the request before it is sent.

Regression test: `muse-code-provider.test.ts` declares `mcp__long_server_name_tool_name_tool_name_tool_name_too_139vuzq6` and expects it unprefixed in the request and as the returned call's name. Without the 64-character rule, the test fails with the 65-character `_mcp__…` name. A live Muse turn that calls `bash` also passes on this commit.

**blocking** — Dropping the `serviceTier !== "flex"` exemption sends Codex `flex` only when discovery lists it, and the Codex catalog never lists it. Upstream `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` (main) advertises `service_tiers: ["priority"]` for every current model (`gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-*`, `gpt-5.5`, `codex-auto-review`), and `[]` for the two daybreak previews. The `codex-discovery.test.ts` fixtures have the same shape. After this change, line 255 returns `false` for `flex` on every Codex model that advertises Fast, so Codex Flex stops working everywhere it was working before. Only the two empty-list previews and rows with no discovered tiers would still get it.

It also goes against the reference client. codex-rs `ModelInfo::supports_service_tier` has `// Flex is an API request option, even when the Codex catalog does not advertise it.` and returns `true` for `flex` no matter what the list says. openai/codex@7abf2a3 (#46230, 2026-09-17) added that on purpose, and its message says: "An explicit `service_tier = "flex"` could be dropped when … the model catalog did not advertise Flex, even though Flex is an API request option." The exemption removed here was written to follow that rule (5d3b33151b0).

The Astra smoke in the PR body shows Flex was left out. It doesn't show that the backend currently rejects `flex` for Astra. If you have a current `Unsupported service_tier: flex` response from a model whose list doesn't include `flex`, please attach it. Without it, this change takes away a working tier.

**blocking:** Anthropic's wire contract limits `fallbacks` to three entries (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic-wire.ts:269-273`), but this maps the entire unbounded setting. A four-model chain is forwarded intact, so Anthropic rejects the request instead of performing fallback. Please reject chains longer than three with a clear configuration error (and document/test the boundary), or deliberately cap them if silent truncation is the intended contract.

Fixed in d65ab5be: the chain is now deliberately capped at the wire limit via ANTHROPIC_MAX_FALLBACK_MODELS = 3 (slice after filtering), with a logger.warn naming the configured vs. forwarded count, the setting description documenting the cap, and a regression test asserting a 5-entry chain forwards exactly the first three. Chose a documented cap over a hard rejection so an overlong config degrades to a working fallback chain instead of failing every Fable request at stream time.

Addressed at the current head (1280e4b0): the mapped chain is deliberately capped at `ANTHROPIC_MAX_FALLBACK_MODELS = 3` (the wire limit) with a `logger.warn` when a configured chain is longer, rather than forwarding it unbounded. Regression test asserts a 5-entry chain forwards exactly the first three.

No content change since the last reply, only a rebase onto upstream v18.1.19 (new commit ids). At the current head (3490b30ab03c): the mapped chain is still deliberately capped at `ANTHROPIC_MAX_FALLBACK_MODELS = 3` (the wire limit) with a `logger.warn` when a configured chain is longer, rather than forwarding it unbounded. Same regression test asserts a 5-entry chain forwards exactly the first three.
